title: A blocking index migration locks the users table and stalls all writes
source_note: Failure pattern (a schema-change migration that takes a blocking lock on a large hot table, stalling every write for its duration) is in the spirit of the GitLab.com 2017 database incident and common online-migration guidance. All services, commit hashes, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~20:11 UTC signups and profile updates are failing with timeouts. Reads look fine. Login mostly works but is slow. A migration deploy went out to users-service just before it started.

signal_lines.msg: migration 20261015 started: CREATE INDEX on users.last_seen_at (table ~80M rows)
lock wait: 40 sessions blocked on AccessExclusiveLock for relation users
write queries to users timing out (statement_timeout 5s); signups and profile updates failing
login succeeded but last_seen_at update timed out; elevated latency
migration cancelled by operator; locks released; writes recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: A schema migration deployed with commit d4e5f6a created an index on users.last_seen_at as a blocking operation on an ~80M-row table. The CREATE INDEX held an AccessExclusiveLock on the users table for its duration, blocking all writes. Every operation that writes to users - signups, profile updates, the last_seen_at touch on login - stalled and hit the 5s statement timeout. Reads were unaffected. Recovery required cancelling the migration to release the lock.
evidence_path: deploy d4e5f6a to users-service at 20:09 ships migration 20261015 (add index on users.last_seen_at)
users-db INFO at 20:10: migration started, CREATE INDEX on an ~80M-row table
users-db WARN: 40+ sessions blocked on AccessExclusiveLock for relation users
users-service write queries time out (statement_timeout 5s); signups and profile updates fail
recovery immediately after the migration is cancelled and locks release
ground_truth.fix: Cancel the blocking migration (done). Re-run it as an online, non-blocking index build (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY). Add a pre-deploy check that flags blocking DDL against large tables and requires an online alternative or a maintenance window.
